title.en: Lesson 1. ㄷ shifts to ㄹ: 듣다 & 걷다

blocks.md:
When certain verbs ending in 받침 **ㄷ** meet an ending starting with a **vowel**, the ㄷ transforms into **ㄹ**.

듣다 (to listen) → 들 + **어요** → **들어요**
걷다 (to walk) → 걸 + **어요** → **걸어요**

In the past tense, the same thing happens: 들 + **었어요** → **들었어요**.

**Not every ㄷ verb changes.** Common regular ones keep their ㄷ:
- **받다** (to receive) → 받아요 / 받았어요 (regular)
- **닫다** (to close) → 닫아요 / 닫았어요 (regular)
- **믿다** (to believe) → 믿어요 / 믿었어요 (regular)

items.tip: I listen to music every day. 듣다 → 들어요
I often walk in the park. 걷다 → 걸어요
I listened to a good song yesterday. 듣다 → 들었어요

blocks.q: How do you conjugate 듣다 (to listen) into the present 해요 form?
blocks.why: ㄷ turns into ㄹ before a vowel, and the vowel ㅡ takes 어요 → **들어요**.

blocks.meaning: I heard that song on the radio yesterday.
blocks.why: 듣다 changes ㄷ to ㄹ before vowels → **들었어요**.

blocks.meaning: The weather was nice, so I walked along the Han River.
blocks.why: 걷다 changes ㄷ to ㄹ before vowels → **걸었어요**.

blocks.q: Which of these verbs does **NOT** change its ㄷ?
blocks.why: **받다** is regular: 받아요 / 받았어요. 듣다 and 걷다 become 들어요 and 걸어요.

blocks.hint: Before a vowel, the ㄷ in 듣다 changes to ㄹ.
blocks.why: 듣다 shifts ㄷ to ㄹ before vowels → **들었어요**.

blocks.q: Translate into Korean: **“I listen to music every day.”**  (every day = 매일, music = 음악, to listen = 듣다)
blocks.hint: Start with 매일, then 음악을, and conjugate 듣다 into 들어요.
blocks.why: 매일 음악을 들어요. 듣다 becomes 들어요.

blocks.q: Say it out loud: “I walk in the park every day.”

title.en: Lesson 2. 르 doubles to ㄹㄹ: 모르다 & 빠르다

blocks.md:
When a verb stem ends in **르**, two things happen before -아/어:
1. The vowel **ㅡ drops out**.
2. An extra **ㄹ attaches underneath** the preceding syllable!

모르다 → 모 + ㄹ + 라요 → **몰라요** (I don’t know)
빠르다 → 빠 + ㄹ + 라요 → **빨라요** (It’s fast)
다르다 → 다 + ㄹ + 라요 → **달라요** (It’s different)

**“잘 몰라요” is one of your primary survival tools in Korea.**

When someone speaks too fast or asks directions: “죄송해요, 저 한국어 잘 몰라요” (Sorry, I don’t know Korean well). Everyone understands immediately.

items.tip: I don’t know Korean well. 모르다 → 몰라요
The subway is really fast. 빠르다 → 빨라요
This and that are different. 다르다 → 달라요

blocks.q: How do you conjugate 모르다 (to not know) into the 해요 form?
blocks.why: 르 loses its ㅡ and adds a ㄹ beneath 모 → **몰라요**.

blocks.meaning: I don’t really know that person’s name.
The subway is much faster than the bus.
blocks.why: 빠르다 doubles the ㄹ to become **빨라요**.

blocks.q: Match each dictionary verb with its 해요 form.
Translate into Korean: **“I don’t know that person well.”**  (that person = 그 사람, well = 잘, to not know = 모르다)
blocks.hint: Use 그 사람(을), the adverb 잘, and conjugate 모르다 into 몰라요.
blocks.why: 그 사람(을) 잘 몰라요. 모르다 conjugates into 몰라요.

blocks.q: Say it out loud: “I don’t know Korean well.”

title.ko: 3강. 르 불규칙의 모음 조화와 꼴 만들기
title.en: Lesson 3. Vowel Harmony in 르-Irregular Verbs

blocks.md:
When a **르** verb meets **-아/어** (like in -아요 / -어요 or -았/었어요), two things happen:

1. **Drop ㅡ** and add a **ㄹ** under the preceding syllable.
2. **Look at the preceding syllable's vowel** to pick the ending:
   - **ㅏ or ㅗ:** add **-라요** (빠르다 → **빨라요**, 모르다 → **몰라요**).
   - **Any other vowel:** add **-러요** (부르다 → **불러요**, 누르다 → **눌러요**, 기르다 → **길러요**).

Remember: before a consonant suffix like **-고** (and) or **-지만** (but), the verb is completely regular:
- 빠르고 (빠르 + 고)
- 모르지만 (모르 + 지만)

items.tip: I sing songs with my friends. (부르다 (ㅜ) → 불러요)
I choose fruit at the shop. (고르다 (ㅗ) → 골라요)

blocks.q: How do you conjugate ‘부르다’ (to sing/call) with the polite ending?
blocks.why: The preceding vowel in 부르다 is ㅜ (not ㅏ or ㅗ), so it takes -러요 → **불러요**. 불라요 has wrong vowel harmony, and 부르어요 fails to apply the irregular rule.

blocks.q: How do you attach -고 (and) to ‘빠르다’ (to be fast)?
blocks.why: The 르 rule only triggers before vowels (-아/어). Before consonants like -고, keep the regular stem: **빠르고**.

blocks.q: Match each 르 verb with its correct polite form.

blocks.meaning: I sing an exciting song at the karaoke room.

blocks.q: Conjugate 고르다 (to pick/choose) into polite present form: 「메뉴에서 음식을 ___ .」
blocks.why: 고 has vowel ㅗ, so it doubles ㄹ and takes -라요 → **골라요**.

blocks.say: 노래방에서 친구와 함께 신나는 노래를 불러요.
blocks.rom: no-rae-bang-e-seo chin-gu-wa ham-kke sin-na-neun no-rae-reul bul-leo-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud: “I sing an exciting song together with my friend at the karaoke room.”

title.en: Lesson 4. Sorting 르-Irregular from Other ㅡ Verbs

blocks.md:
Be careful not to confuse **르-irregular verbs** with verbs that simply end in **ㅡ**:

- **르 verbs (모르다, 빠르다):** Drop ㅡ **AND add an extra ㄹ** → **몰라요**, **빨라요**.
- **Regular ㅡ verbs (쓰다, 끄다, 크다, 아프다):** Just drop ㅡ, **no extra ㄹ** → **써요**, **꺼요**, **커요**, **아파요**.
- Exception to know: **따르다** (to follow / to pour) follows the simple ㅡ drop: **따라요** (not 딸라요)!

blocks.md: Look at **아프다**! It ends in ㅡ, but the letter before it is ㅍ, not ㄹ. So it is just a plain ㅡ drop: **머리가 아파요** (not 머리가 알파요).

items.tip: I turn off the light in the room. (끄다 is plain ㅡ drop → 꺼요)
My throat hurts from a cold. (아프다 is plain ㅡ drop → 아파요)
Water and oil are different from each other. (다르다 is 르-irregular → 달라요)

blocks.q: Which verb adds an extra ㄹ before -아요/-어요?
blocks.why: 다르다 is a 르-irregular verb (달라요). 아프다 (아파요), 쓰다 (써요), and 끄다 (꺼요) are plain ㅡ drop verbs.

blocks.q: How do you conjugate ‘끄다’ (to turn off) with -어요?
blocks.why: 끄다 is a plain ㅡ drop verb, not a 르 verb. Drop ㅡ and attach -어요 → **꺼요**.

blocks.q: Match each verb with its conjugated polite form.

blocks.meaning: The colors of the two clothes are completely different.
blocks.why: 다르다 has vowel ㅏ before 르, so it becomes **달라요**.

blocks.q: Conjugate 다르다 (to be different) into polite present form: 「저와 생각이 ___ .」
blocks.why: 다르다 adds a ㄹ beneath 다 and takes -라요 → **달라요**.

blocks.q: Read out loud contrasting the uncontracted 다르고 and the contracted 달라요.
